title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and with a light agenda took little time to conduct the bi-monthly meeting.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and opened the floor to public comment.  The first to speak was Herb Henson representing Flora Rotary Club.  With the public restroom completed, the group would now like to move forward with the construction of a rain shelter/pavilion at the Pickleball Courts.  Henson said they have met with the interested parties and intend to follow their standard agreement of Rotary providing labor and the city helping with supplies.  Henson estimated the new building will cost between $19,000 and $20,000 with materials purchased through Flora Lumber Supply.  Commissioners approved the measure on a unanimous vote.

Next, Nicky Green with Flora Tourism’s Community Market asked the council to approve their Back to School Bash on Saturday, August 15 at Library Park.  The request also includes closing E. 2nd St. during the event.  Among the activities planned are a biscuit and gravy fundraiser, Rotary Club Workshop, vendors, back to school haircuts, food trucks and a foam party from 11:00-Noon.  Green also asked about displaying a 4’ x 8’ banner encouraging people to attend.  It would be placed along Route 50 near the intersection with N. State Street, where the large American Flag is displayed during holidays.  Mayor Spicer asked Green to coordinate with Toby Rinehart and IDOT.  Commissioners approved her request without dissent.  Green also requested permission for Flora Tourism to host Ford Town in downtown Flora on Friday and Saturday September 18 and 19.  The group uses North Avenue and 2nd Street in the downtown area and the council gave its blessing in a unanimous vote and asked the group to coordinate both events with Flora Police.

Next Flora resident Anthony Krutsinger spoke briefly to the council for a third time concerning the use of Flock Cameras to monitor vehicle traffic along certain roadways.  Krutsinger said he was taking pictures in the middle of the street on July 21st and someone reported him for trespassing to the police department.  He stated he was on public property and not private property so he could not have been trespassing.  Krutsinger reported that the responding officer mentioned to someone that Krutsinger hadn’t gotten the message.  Krutsinger questioned what message he was supposed to have received.  He turned to Asst. Police Chief Greenwood and asked him the question again, but Greenwood said he didn’t know of any message.  Krutsinger stated there was no violation and ended his remarks.

Mayor Spicer asked for a motion to approve the agenda and consent agenda and both items were approved by commissioners.  The latter included past meeting minutes and the warrant list for the last half of July.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer began by thanking Commissioner Lacey Lewis for filling in for her at the previous meeting.  She also congratulated the Clay County Fair Board for a successful event last week that even included fireworks as the conclusion of the queen pageant Friday night.  The mayor asked for a motion to reimburse Clip And Tip Strays or CATS, up to $2,000 for the submission of eligible receipts for spay and neuter expenses of stray cats in the Flora city limits.  A motion was made and approved unanimously.  Next, commissioners approved an ordinance for a TIF (Tax Increment Financing) Redevelopment Plan for concrete in front of Floyd Henson Junior High School in the amount of $49,681.  The council also approved a resolution for an engineering agreement with Milano & Grunloh Engineers of Effingham for additional Safe Routes to School sidewalk construction in the amount of $31,130.

Mayor Spicer then polled commissioners for their comments.  Commissioner Phil Wiley once again thanked NAL and others for the free swim events this summer at the Flora Swimming Pool.  He also thanked everyone involved with the Clay County Fair and what a great week it was except for the rainfall on Monday.  He noted the mild weather had a positive impact on fair attendance, and he said he talk with Joe Goodman about the 4-H BBQ and the rodeo on Friday and said they had the best crowd ever.  Wiley closed with a reminder that school is about to start up in a couple of weeks and urged everyone to be on the lookout for school kids and to be ready for the change in traffic patterns.

Commissioner Lacey Lewis asked commissioners to approve the hiring of Steve Pride as a temporary janitor for the Flora Volunteer Fire Department at a cost of $332 per month, effective August 4.  The motion was approved without dissent.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles asked commissioners to approve an ordinance approving the sale of real estate at 717 N. State St.  The measure was approved unanimously.  With all business concluded, the meeting adjourned.

title: CISNE REUNION
full_story:
A full schedule of events kicks-off tomorrow at the 2026 Cisne Reunion.  Opening ceremonies and the introduction of Hilda Smith, this year’s parade marshal will take place at 6:30 pm.  The Kingsmen will be the opening night performers at 7pm.  This years Cisne Reunion event pays tribute to the Cisne High School Class of 1976 on their 50th reunion and the Class of 2001 on their 25th reunion.

Thursday, in addition to Bingo from 7 to 9 pm, the pageants will take center stage.  There will be the Tiny Tot, Little Miss, Junior Miss, and Miss Cisne Reunion pageants.

Friday, in addition to Bingo from 7 to 9 pm, Jake Perry and Hayden Brown will take the stage in the park at 7 pm.

Saturday will begin with race day registration and a community breakfast at the Community Center.  Race day Registration begins at 6 am on stage in the square, and the breakfast is from 7 to 10 am.

The 1 mile Fun Run is set to begin at 7:30 am, with the 15th annual 5K Run, Walk to begin at 8 am.  Tractor Show setup is from 8 to 10 am.  Car show registration begins at 9 am with awards at 12:30 pm, and the tractor show is at 10:30.  Kids’ Games and a FFA Petting Zoo on the square will be from 10 to Noon.  There will be a kids pedal pull at Noon on the square.  The annual parade lineup is at 2 pm at the high school with the parade at 2:30 pm.  Bill Atwood will serve as master of ceremonies for the Cisne Reunion parade.

The Ashes will perform from 4 to 6 pm, bingo will run from 5 to 9 pm and the Reunion closes with a performance by Duke Boys on the main stage at 7 pm.

title: HUDSON AT WORLD COMPETITION
full_story:
Flora High School student Paul Hudson competed at the Microsoft World Competition July 26th through 29th in Anaheim, California.

Hudson earned this opportunity by winning first place in excel at the Microsoft National Competition in June in Nashville.  He was also the state champion in excel for Illinois.  Thirty-five countries participated at the world competition.  Paul placed fourth at the world competition.

Paul Hudson was accompanied by his parents David and Sara Hudson.

title: WAYNE COUNTY DEATH
full_story:
An accident Saturday afternoon claimed the life of a rural Mount Erie woman.

Mandy L. Fox, 46, was inside a box trailer sorting lumber for a house she was remodeling when a stack of wood fell on her.  Family members said her boyfriend found her unresponsive beneath the lumber and called for help.  She was taken to Fairfield Memorial Hospital and airlifted to an Evansville hospital where she was pronounced dead.

The scene of the accident was at a wooded lot southwest of Mt. Erie.

title: MARION COUNTY CHILD DIES
full_story:
Fayette County Coroner David Harris announced Sunday that a three-year-old child was a drowning victim in Fayette County.

Fayette County Sheriff Ronnie Stevens contacted Coroner Harris Friday evening regarding the child’s death.  Coroner Harris said the child was from Centralia, but the incident occurred at a rural Fayette County residence.  The child was transported to Sarah Bush Lincoln Fayette County Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

The Coroner’s report says that due to the ongoing investigation by the his Office and the Sheriff’s Office no further information is being released at this time.  He said that the manner of death was accidental.

title: WILHOUR TRAVELING OFFICE HOURS
full_story:

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is accepting sponsorships for their 28th annual golf scramble to be held on Friday, August 14th.

The Chamber offers a variety of sponsorship opportunities to suit every budget.  From Gold Sponsorship at $400 to the affordable Bronze Sponsorship at $50, there’s an option for everyone to get involved and showcase their support for the Flora business community.

Team registration is $50 per person or $200 per team.  Entry fee includes 4 drink tickets courtesy of the Flora Bank and Trust a goodie bag with a sleeve of balls and lunch courtesy of the Flora Savings Bank.  There will also be mulligans, 4 foot strings, and yellow tee boxes, for $20 each or $50 for all 3.

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm.

To register your team call Arriel Dulaney at the Flora Chamber of Commerce at 618-662-5646.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Statewide, the USDA says 60% of the corn crop is in good to excellent condition, with 94% silking and 47% in dough stage, both in line with the average pace, while 58% of soybeans are in good shape with 88% blooming and 62% setting pods.  The Illinois winter wheat harvest is complete.

The USDA reported Monday that there were 5.1 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending August 2nd.  Statewide, the average temperature was 75.4 degrees, .2 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.77 inches, 0.83 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 14% short, 73% adequate, and 8% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 6% very short, 22% short, 64% adequate, and 8% surplus.

Corn silking reached 94%, even with the 5-year average.  Corn dough reached 47%, even with the 5-year average.  Corn dented reached 3%, compared to the 5-year average of 2%.  Corn condition was rated 2% very poor, 9% poor, 29% fair, 47% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 88%, compared to the 5-year average of 87%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 62%, compared to the 5-year average of 61%.  Soybeans condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 31% fair, 48% good, and 10% excellent.

title: FMH SCHOOL SPORT PHYSICALS
full_story:
